cards.q: What is a static EtherChannel (`mode on`)?
cards.a: A static EtherChannel bundles multiple physical interfaces into one logical Port-channel without using LACP or PAgP negotiation. Both ends must be configured consistently because there is no negotiation.

cards.q: What happens when a port is configured with channel-group 1 mode on?
cards.a: It creates/uses EtherChannel 1, does NOT negotiate, and treats the configured member ports as one bundle. There is no active/passive/desirable/auto state.

cards.q: Which EtherChannel mode combinations form a static on bundle?
cards.a: ON + ON = static EtherChannel. ON + LACP = no negotiated bundle; ON + PAgP = no negotiated bundle.

cards.q: Why must both ends of a static EtherChannel be configured as on?
cards.a: Because a static EtherChannel has no protocol (no LACP/PAgP PDUs) with which to negotiate compatibility; the switch relies entirely on the administrator's configuration, so one side on and the other LACP/PAgP does not form a bundle.

cards.q: Does static EtherChannel send LACP or PAgP PDUs?
cards.a: No. Static on sends no LACP PDUs, no PAgP PDUs, and performs no negotiation.

cards.q: When is static on a reasonable choice?
cards.a: When the peer device does not support LACP/PAgP, when a no-negotiation bundle is explicitly required, or in lab/learning environments. For normal modern switch-to-switch deployments, prefer LACP.

cards.q: Why should LACP be preferred over static on for modern switch-to-switch deployments?
cards.a: LACP is an IEEE standard with multi-vendor support, performs negotiation, and provides better operational safety through negotiation than a static non-negotiated bundle.

cards.q: Does static on bypass EtherChannel member-compatibility requirements?
cards.a: No. You still need compatible speed, duplex, switchport mode, access/native VLAN, allowed VLANs, trunk configuration, Layer-3 configuration, and same EtherChannel grouping where applicable.

cards.q: How does STP view a correctly formed static EtherChannel?
cards.a: STP sees one logical port rather than treating the individual member links as separate parallel STP paths.

cards.q: Does STP always see one port just because `mode on` is configured?
cards.a: No. The one-STP-port behavior depends on the EtherChannel being correctly formed. An incorrectly configured bundle can cause blocked links, connectivity problems, or, in a bad topology, a Layer-2 loop. Never assume mode on makes an unsafe topology safe.

cards.q: How does static EtherChannel do load balancing?
cards.a: It uses the same general EtherChannel load-balancing mechanism as LACP and PAgP: a hash (e.g., port-channel load-balance src-dst-ip) selects a physical member per flow.

cards.q: Does a static 4×1-Gbps EtherChannel give a single flow 4 Gbps?
cards.a: No. It provides about 4-Gbps aggregate capacity across multiple flows, but a single flow typically uses one member.

cards.q: In `show etherchannel summary`, what do SU and P mean?
cards.a: S = Layer-2 EtherChannel; U = in use; P = port is bundled in the port-channel. P does not mean PAgP.

cards.q: Which commands verify a static EtherChannel?
cards.a: show etherchannel summary; show etherchannel 1 detail or show etherchannel 1 port-channel; show interfaces port-channel 1; show interfaces status; show etherchannel load-balance.

cards.q: What is the troubleshooting workflow for a static EtherChannel?
cards.a: Check physical interfaces → verify both sides use static on → show etherchannel summary → check member consistency → show interfaces port-channel 1 → check STP → check load balancing.

cards.q: What is the main risk of a static EtherChannel?
cards.a: There is no protocol negotiation to detect an incompatible peer configuration, so configuration mismatch is the main risk. Both ends must be manually consistent.

cards.q: What is the most important CCNP static-on rule?
cards.a: ON + ON = STATIC ETHERCHANNEL; ON + LACP = NO NEGOTIATED BUNDLE; ON + PAgP = NO NEGOTIATED BUNDLE; LACP = MODERN IEEE STANDARD; PAgP = CISCO PROPRIETARY; ON = STATIC / NO NEGOTIATION.

cards.q: What are the key static-`on` quick-review facts?
cards.a: mode on = no LACP/no PAgP/no negotiation; both ends must be on; members must be compatible; no negotiation means less protection against config errors; correctly formed bundle appears as one STP port; LACP preferred for modern deployments.
